findings.title: Required authoring Context has no supported minting carrier
findings.cause: The new builder and narrowing require a governed Context pointer, but the existing callable minting API only constructs Context from parent and typed artifacts.
evidence: Builder lines 18-19 require preservation of authoring-owner in every governed Context; narrowing lines 7-8 repeats that quality criterion.

docs/custom-workflow-authoring.md opening paragraph requires the exact owner path in sealed Context, and the frozen plan's Authoring intake acceptance explicitly requires this carriage to planner and maker.
scripts/tickets_mint.py:184 _context only emits parent and artifact clauses; :254 _minted always uses that result as Context. :301-302 accepts goal-file/details-file, without a Context input.

Read-only probe intercepted _mint with the owner supplied in both Goal and Details: minted Context was exactly '- parent: B1', without the owner. The callable parser independently returned 'do does not accept --context-file'. Probe exited 0 after asserting these observations; no state was created.

The global authoring narrowing does link the canonical guide, so this is a precise unmet carrier obligation, not evidence that the guide is unreachable or a claim that every authoring child behaves incorrectly.
findings.smallest_remedy: Provide one supported pre-seal Context carrier in callable minting and thread it through the authoring call, preserving existing Context ownership and seals; test owner preservation through the emitted ticket. Any alternative must reconcile the canonical owner requirement as well as the builder, rather than silently placing a different heading inside Goal.
findings.scope: Runtime/API repair exceeds this review-only ticket. The implementation plan permits a scoped core repair only after a reproduced seam failure; this probe supplies that failure for a separately assigned repair.

findings.title: New public workflow is missing existing inventory integrations
findings.cause: The new shipped public name was added to installer discovery and new tests but not to every existing census/catalog owner.
evidence: Direct source inspection: tests/test_ticket_frames.py:793 hardcodes self.assertEqual(8 + 2, len(self.bodies)), while the comprehension collects both existing workflow homes and therefore includes the new builder.

Reviewer independently ran FrameLawOwnerTest, test_static_tree_invariants and test_cell_linter together: exit 1, 52 tests in 51.551 seconds, five failures. Three fail at the frame census (10 != 11), one at tests/test_static_tree_invariants_cases/compositions.py:45 missing builder in WORKFLOWS, and one at :76 whose predicate accepts only a literal --standard or nested frame-open command. No cell-linter failure occurred at this fixed source identity.

Root independently reports the full source suite at the integration gate: 2177 tests, 6 failures. Three are FrameLawOwnerTest's hardcoded census; two are static_tree_invariants' workflow allowlist and nested-frame assumption; one is TestScriptNames.test_build_plan_installs_every_managed_script_with_matching_content from installed reader project_workflow_catalog rejecting workflow-summary-manifest.json coverage.

Root reports the static-tree nested-frame predicate requires a literal nested frame, whereas the new builder lawfully uses checkpointed-build's ordinary public call. Repair the check's representation of the seam, not the lawful composition by introducing a redundant wrapper.
The full-suite count and installed-reader manifest failure remain explicitly parent-provided observations; the five census/composition failures were independently reproduced here.
findings.smallest_remedy: Reconcile the public workflow summary/catalog owners and existing census checks with the newly shipped name; make composition coverage recognize the actual public call. Derive inventory where appropriate rather than replacing 10 with another brittle count. Keep a can-fail reading for the retained contract.

positive_assessment: The authoring procedure inventories existing primitives, methods, workflows and standards, explicitly admits a useful first-use independent contract, and orders top-down decomposition with bottom-up verification. It does not impose a depth quota.
The public builder supplies every checkpointed-build semantic input, adds distinct authoring/live-admission responsibility, and does not copy its plan/wave/judge/repair mechanics.
The authoring standard is a global narrowing of orch-code, so another public workflow can resolve it; the deterministic chain is broad-to-narrow and deduplicated.
The produced receipt fixture preserves its top-level standard in a clone of accepted source, respecting the public callee scope. It does not manufacture private wrappers.
The builder returns fixed package identity, independent findings and runtime evidence. Its Never and partial-result clauses prevent static checks from becoming a live success claim.
No implementation or public contract was changed by this reviewer. Source changes are narrowly concentrated in authoring documentation, the builder, its narrowing, a fixture and related tests.
